title: Human Reproduction
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Human Reproduction Worksheets (Fertilisation, Gestation, Placenta)
standard_text: Reproduction in humans (as an example of a mammal), including the structure and function of the male and female reproductive systems, menstrual cycle (without details of hormones), gametes, fertilisation, gestation and birth, to include the effect of maternal lifestyle on the foetus through the placenta.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on human reproduction: the reproductive systems, gametes, fertilisation, the menstrual cycle, gestation, the placenta and the effect of lifestyle on the foetus. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A sperm and an egg join at fertilisation.
key_sub: The placenta feeds the foetus, but harmful substances can cross it too.
body_html:
How to think about it

Humans reproduce sexually: a sperm cell and an egg cell join at fertilisation.

  • Testes make sperm; ovaries release an egg about once a month. Fertilisation happens in the oviduct.
  • The embryo implants in the uterus. The placenta passes oxygen and nutrients to the foetus and takes away waste.
  • Gestation lasts about 9 months. Smoking, alcohol and some drugs can cross the placenta and harm the foetus.
Example

Where does fertilisation happen?

The egg travels along it

Answer: the oviduct

Example

What does the placenta give the foetus?

From the mother's blood

Answer: oxygen and nutrients

Common mistakes

  • Thinking fertilisation happens in the uterus.
  • Thinking the placenta blocks everything harmful.
  • Thinking eggs are made in the uterus.

faq.a: In the oviduct. The fertilised egg then moves to the uterus and attaches to its lining.
It passes oxygen and nutrients from the mother's blood to the foetus and takes carbon dioxide and waste away. Alcohol, nicotine and some drugs can also cross it.
